1.word_for_word: चत्वारिंशे ततोऽक्रूरः कृष्णं मत्वेश्वरेश्वरम् । — In the forty-fourth century, Akrūra considered Kṛṣṇa to be the Lord of all lords.; प्रणम्य भक्त्या तुष्टाव स-गुणागुण-भेदतः ॥ — He bowed down to the Lord with devotion and satisfied Him by distinguishing His qualities.; श्री-कृष्णं प्रणमति---नतोऽस्मीति । — He bows down to Sri Krishna, saying, “I bow down.”; हे कृष्ण ! — O Krishna!; त्वा त्वां नतोऽस्मि । — I bow to you, you.; त्वम् अस्मत्-पितृव्यः कुतो मां बालं नतोऽसि ? — Why do you, our father-in-law, bow down to me as a child?; तत्राह---आद्यं पुरुषम् अव्ययं च । — There he argues that the first person is the infinitive.; अनादि-निधनम् इत्य् अर्थः । — It means eternal death.; कुत एतत् ? — Where is this?; अखिल-हेतूनां हेतुम् । — The cause of all causes.; स तु नारायणो नाहम् इति चेत्, तत्राह---नारायणं त्वाम् । — But if he says, “I am not Nārāyaṇa,” then he says, “I am Nārāyaṇa.”; किं नारायण इति मां स्तौषि ? — Are you praising me as Narayana?; काद्यं स्तुतिः सत्यम् एवेत्य् आह---यन् नाभि-जाताद् इति । — He argues that the first praise is true, because it is from the navel.; यतो ब्रह्मणः ॥१॥ — Because of the Brahman.
1.translation: In the forty-fourth century, Akrūra considered Kṛṣṇa to be the Lord of all lords. He bowed down to the Lord with devotion and satisfied Him by distinguishing His qualities. He bows down to Sri Krishna, saying, “I bow down.” O Krishna! I bow to you, you. Why do you, our father-in-law, bow down to me as a child? There he argues that the first person is the infinitive. It means eternal death. Where is this? The cause of all causes. But if he says, “I am not Nārāyaṇa,” then he says, “I am Nārāyaṇa.” Are you praising me as Narayana? He argues that the first praise is true, because it is from the navel. Because of the Brahman.

2.word_for_word: अखिल-हेतु-हेतुत्वं प्रपञ्चयति---भूर् इति । — He argues that the cause of all causes is the earth.; खस्यादिर् अहङ्कारः । — The origin of the sky is ego.; अजा माया । — Aja Maya.; तस्या आदिः पुरुषः । — Her original man is the man.; एते ये जगतो हेतवः, ते सर्वे तवाङ्ग-भूताः । — All these causes of the universe are part of You.; अङ्गाच् छ्री-मूर्तेर् भूताः उपसर्जन-भूता वा ॥२॥ — From the limbs of the form of the goddess of fortune are the beings or the beings of the prepositions.
2.translation: He argues that the cause of all causes is the earth. The origin of the sky is ego. Aja Maya. Her original man is the man. All these causes of the universe are part of You. From the limbs of the form of the goddess of fortune are the beings or the beings of the prepositions.

3.word_for_word:
नन्व् अति-स्तुतिः कथं क्रियते, अहम् एवान्यत उत्पन्नस् तत् पर-तन्त्रश् चेत्य् आशङ्क्य, तवैषा माया, त्वत्-पारमार्थ्यं तु न कोऽपि वेदेत्य् आह---नैत इति । — Now, how can over-praise be done? Doubting that I myself have arisen from another place and that it is the system of others, he argues that this is Your illusion, but no one knows Your transcendence.; एते अज आदिर् येषां ते आत्मनस् ते स्वरूपं न विदुः । — These are the unborn and the beginning of the universe, and they do not know the nature of the Self.; अनात्मतया जडत्वेन कारणेन । — Because of its unselfishness and dullness.; जडत्वे हेतुः, गृहीताः प्रत्यक्षादिभिर् दृष्टाः । — The cause of dullness is that they are seen by direct perception and other means.; न ह्य् अजादो दृग्-गोचर इति भावः । — This means that the unborn is not visible.; ननु जडा मां मा जानन्तु जीवस् तु ज्ञास्यतीत्य् अत आह---अज इति । — Indeed, let the dull not know Me, but the living will know Me.; सोऽजो ब्रह्माऽप्य् अजाया गुणैर् अनुबद्ध आवृतो गुणातीतं ते तव स्वरूपं न वेद, अन्यः कुतो ज्ञास्यतीति । — That unborn Brahman, who is bound and covered by the modes of nature, does not know Your transcendental nature, and how can anyone else know?; यद्वा प्रकृत्य्-आदय आत्मनः स्वरूपं तव स्वरूपं च न विदुः, जडत्वाद् एव । — In other words, nature and others do not know the nature of the Self and Your nature, because they are dull.; जीवस् तु तानात्मानं च वेत्ति न पुनस् त्वत्-स्वरूपम् इति । — The living entity, however, knows them and himself, not again as your form.; यथोक्तं हंस-गुह्ये--- — As stated in the Hans-guhye; > देहोऽसवोऽक्षा मनवो भूत-मात्रा >
> नात्मानम् अन्यं च विदुः परं यत् । — > The body, the senses, the axes, the Manus, the beings, the matter >
> They do not know themselves or anything else beyond that.; >
> सर्वं पुमान् वेद गुणांश् च तज्-ज्ञो >
> न वेद सर्व-ज्ञम् अनन्तम् ईडे ॥ — >
> Every man knows the qualities and is knower of them >
> I worship the omniscient, infinite, who does not know.; [६.४.२५] इति ॥३॥ — [6.4.25] It is.
3.translation:
Now, how can over-praise be done? Doubting that I myself have arisen from another place and that it is the system of others, he argues that this is Your illusion, but no one knows Your transcendence. These are the unborn and the beginning of the universe, and they do not know the nature of the Self. Because of its unselfishness and dullness. The cause of dullness is that they are seen by direct perception and other means. This means that the unborn is not visible. Indeed, let the dull not know Me, but the living will know Me. That unborn Brahman, who is bound and covered by the modes of nature, does not know Your transcendental nature, and how can anyone else know? In other words, nature and others do not know the nature of the Self and Your nature, because they are dull. The living entity, however, knows them and himself, not again as your form. As stated in the Hans-guhye > The body, the senses, the axes, the Manus, the beings, the matter >
> They do not know themselves or anything else beyond that. >
> Every man knows the qualities and is knower of them >
> I worship the omniscient, infinite, who does not know. [6.4.25] It is.

4.word_for_word: ननु यदि केऽपि न जानन्ति कथं तर्हि संसार-निवृत्तिर् जीवानाम् ? — Indeed, if no one knows how, then, can living beings cease from the world?; इत्य् आशङ्क्य साक्षाद् अगोचरत्वेऽपि येन केनापि मार्गेण भजतां त्वं गम्योऽसीत्य् आह---त्वां योगिन इति । — Doubting this, he said, “You are accessible to those who worship You by any means, even though You are directly invisible.”; हैरण्य-गर्भादयोऽध्यात्माधिभूताधिदैव-साक्षिणं महा-पुरुषं तद् अन्तर्यामि-स्वरूपम् ईश्वरं नियन्तारं च यजन्ति ॥४॥ — The Hiraṇya-garbhas and others worship that Supreme Personality of Godhead, the witness of the Supreme Soul, the Supersoul, the Supersoul and the Supersoul, who is the innermost form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and who is the controller of all.
4.translation: Indeed, if no one knows how, then, can living beings cease from the world? Doubting this, he said, “You are accessible to those who worship You by any means, even though You are directly invisible.” The Hiraṇya-garbhas and others worship that Supreme Personality of Godhead, the witness of the Supreme Soul, the Supersoul, the Supersoul and the Supersoul, who is the innermost form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and who is the controller of all.

5.word_for_word: तद् एवं साङ्ख्य-योगावेकी-कृत्योक्तौ, त्रयी-मार्गं कर्म-ज्ञान-भेदेन दर्शयति---त्रय्या चेति श्लोक-द्वयेन । — That is why, in the statement of the Sāṅkhya-yoga-veki-kṛti, he shows the path of the Trinity by the distinction between karma and knowledge in two verses: Trinity and.; वैतानिकाः कर्म-योगिनस् त्वां वै त्वाम् एव यजन्ते । — The Vaitanikas, the karma-yogis, worship You alone.; ननु ते इन्द्र-वरुण-वाय्व्-आदीन् यजन्ते, नतु माम् इत्य् अत आह---नाना वज्र-हस्तादीनि रूपाणि येषां ते येऽमरास् तेषाम् आख्यया नाम्ना त्वाम् एव यजन्त इति । — Indeed, they worship Indra, Varuna, Vayu and others, but not Me. Therefore he argues that the immortals who have various forms such as Vajra and Hasta worship You by the name of these immortals.; अयं भावः---ऐन्द्र-वारुणादि-सूक्तैर् इन्द्रादयः सर्वैश्वर्येण प्राकाश्यन्ते न च सर्वेश्वरा बहवः सम्भवन्ति, अतो नाम-भेदेन त्वाम् एव यजन्त इति । — This means that by the Suktas of Indra and Varuna, Indra and others are revealed in all their opulence, and that there are not many Lords of all, and therefore they worship You alone by difference of names.; तथा च श्रुतिः---स प्रथमः स प्रकृतिर् विश्व-कर्मा, स प्रथमो मित्रा-वरुणोऽग्निः, स प्रथमो बृहस्पतिश् चिकित्वान्, तस्मा इन्द्राय हविर् आजुहोतिइति ॥५॥ — Similarly, the scriptures say, "That first nature is Visva-karma, that first Mitra-Varuna is the fire, that first Brihaspati is the healer, and therefore he offers oblations to Indra.
5.translation: That is why, in the statement of the Sāṅkhya-yoga-veki-kṛti, he shows the path of the Trinity by the distinction between karma and knowledge in two verses: Trinity and. The Vaitanikas, the karma-yogis, worship You alone. Indeed, they worship Indra, Varuna, Vayu and others, but not Me. Therefore he argues that the immortals who have various forms such as Vajra and Hasta worship You by the name of these immortals. This means that by the Suktas of Indra and Varuna, Indra and others are revealed in all their opulence, and that there are not many Lords of all, and therefore they worship You alone by difference of names. Similarly, the scriptures say, "That first nature is Visva-karma, that first Mitra-Varuna is the fire, that first Brihaspati is the healer, and therefore he offers oblations to Indra.

6.word_for_word: ज्ञान-यज्ञेन समाधिना ॥६॥ — By the sacrifice of knowledge and meditation.
6.translation: By the sacrifice of knowledge and meditation.

7.word_for_word: साङ्ख्य-योग-त्रयी-मार्गा उक्ताः, वैष्णव-शैव-मार्गावाह् द्वयेन, अन्ये चेति । — The paths of Sāṅkhya, Yoga and Trayi have been mentioned, the Vaishnava and Shaiva paths by two, and others.; संस्कृतात्मानो वैष्णव-शैवदी-क्षया दीक्षिताः सन्तः ते त्वयाभिहितेन पञ्च-रात्रादि-विधिना त्वन्-मयास् त्वन्-मयत्वेनात्मनं चिन्तयन्तस् त्वद्-एक-प्रधाना इति वा । — The Sanskrit souls, who have been initiated into the Vaiṣṇava and Śaivadi disciplines, by the five-night-like rituals prescribed by You, are called Mayas, who think of themselves as Yours, or who are predominantly You alone.; वासुदेव-सङ्कर्षण-प्रद्युम्नानिरुद्ध-भेदेन बहु-मूर्तिं नारायण-रूपेणैक-मूर्तिकं च त्वाम् एव यजन्ति ॥७॥ — They worship You alone, who have many forms in the form of Nārāyaṇa and who are distinguished from Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha.
7.translation: The paths of Sāṅkhya, Yoga and Trayi have been mentioned, the Vaishnava and Shaiva paths by two, and others. The Sanskrit souls, who have been initiated into the Vaiṣṇava and Śaivadi disciplines, by the five-night-like rituals prescribed by You, are called Mayas, who think of themselves as Yours, or who are predominantly You alone. They worship You alone, who have many forms in the form of Nārāyaṇa and who are distinguished from Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha.

8.word_for_word: बह्व्-आचार्य-विभेदेनेति नाना-भेद-शैव-पाशुपतादि-मार्गेण ॥८॥ — By the difference of many teachers, that is, by the path of various differences, such as Shiva, Pashupata and others.
8.translation: By the difference of many teachers, that is, by the path of various differences, such as Shiva, Pashupata and others.

9.word_for_word: येऽपि क्षुद्र-देवता-भक्तास् तेऽपि त्वाम् एव यजन्तीत्य् आह---सर्व एवेति । — He argues that even those who are devotees of insignificant deities worship You alone.; हे सर्व-देव-मय ! — O all-godly!; नन्व् एते परस्पर-देवताधिक्षेप-कलह-व्याकुल-चित्ताः कथम् एकम् एव यजन्तीत्य् उच्यते ? — How, then, can it be said that these people, whose minds are troubled by mutual blasphemy, quarreling, and disturbance, sacrifice to one another?; तत्राह---यद्यप्य् अन्य-धिय इति । — There he argues that although other-minded.; बुद्धि-मात्र-भेदो न वस्तु-भेद इत्य् अर्थः ॥९॥ — This means that the difference is merely intellectual and not objective.
9.translation: He argues that even those who are devotees of insignificant deities worship You alone. O all-godly! How, then, can it be said that these people, whose minds are troubled by mutual blasphemy, quarreling, and disturbance, sacrifice to one another? There he argues that although other-minded. This means that the difference is merely intellectual and not objective.

10.word_for_word: तस्मात् सर्वे मार्गास् त्वय्य् एव पर्यवस्यन्तीति सदृष्टान्तम् आह---यथेति । — Therefore, he gives a good example of how all paths lead to you.; अद्रेः सकाशात् सर्वतः प्रभवन्ति या नद्यस् ताः पुनः पर्जन्येनापूरिता बहु-स्रोतसः सत्यः सर्वतः सिन्धुम् एव विशन्ति यथा, तद्वद् एता गतयो मार्गा अन्ततस् त्वाम् एव विशन्तीति ॥१०॥ — The rivers which flow from all sides near the mountains, filled with rain again, are of many streams and truly enter the sea from all sides, so these paths of movement eventually enter You.
10.translation: Therefore, he gives a good example of how all paths lead to you. The rivers which flow from all sides near the mountains, filled with rain again, are of many streams and truly enter the sea from all sides, so these paths of movement eventually enter You.

11.word_for_word: अत्र हेतुम् आह---सत्त्वम् इति । — The reason here is that it is the essence.; भवतः शक्तिर् या प्रकृतिस् तस्याः सत्त्वादयो गुणा अतः प्राकृताः प्रकृति-कारोपाधयो ब्रह्म-पर्यन्ताः स्थावरादयो जीवाः स्वोपाधि-द्वारा तेषु गुणेषु प्रोताः प्रविष्टास् ते च प्रकृतौ सा च त्वयीति । — Your power, which is nature, has its qualities, such as Sattva. Therefore, the ordinary beings, who are the subjects of nature and the causes of nature, up to Brahman, and the living entities, such as the immovable, are woven into those qualities by their own subjects.; अतः क्रमेणोपाधि-लयात् सर्वेऽपि त्वाम् एव विशन्तीति । — Therefore, gradually, from the rhythm of the title, everyone enters into You.; यद्वा भवतः प्रकृतेर् गुणेषु प्रोता ब्रह्मादयो भवद् व्यतिरिक्ता न सन्ति, अतस् त्वम् एव सर्व-देव-मय इति ॥११॥ — That is, Brahma and others, who are immersed in the modes of nature of Your nature, do not exist apart from You, therefore You alone are the embodiment of all the gods.
11.translation: The reason here is that it is the essence. Your power, which is nature, has its qualities, such as Sattva. Therefore, the ordinary beings, who are the subjects of nature and the causes of nature, up to Brahman, and the living entities, such as the immovable, are woven into those qualities by their own subjects. Therefore, gradually, from the rhythm of the title, everyone enters into You. That is, Brahma and others, who are immersed in the modes of nature of Your nature, do not exist apart from You, therefore You alone are the embodiment of all the gods.

12.word_for_word: ननु भवतः प्रकृतेर् इति वदन् ममापि प्रकृति-सम्बन्धं ब्रवीषि । — Indeed, by saying that you are of nature, you are also speaking of my relationship with nature.; ततश् च तेषां मम चको विशेषः स्याद् इत्य् आशङ्क्य विशेषम् आह---तुभ्यम् इति । — Then, fearing that my chaka might be special to them, he said specially to you.; अविभक्त-दृष्टयेऽलिप्त-बुद्धये । — For undivided vision and untainted intelligence.; कुतः ? — Where is it from?; सर्वात्मने स्व-व्यतिरिक्ताभावाद् अविषक्त-दृष्टित्वम् इत्य् अर्थः । — This means that the whole self is unattached to the self, since it is not separate from itself.; किं च सर्व-धियां साक्षिणे । — What about the witness of all intelligence?; सर्व-बुद्धि-साक्षित्वान् न क्वापि बुद्धि-लेप इत्य् अर्थः । — This means that there is no ointment of intelligence anywhere because it is the witness of all intelligence.; इतरे तु संसरन्तीत्य् आह---गुण-प्रवाह इति । — Others, he argues, are transmitted by the flow of the modes.; देव-नृ-तिर्यं च आत्मानो येषां तेषु देवादि-शरीराभिमानिष्व् इत्य् अर्थः । — This means that in those whose souls are demigods, human beings and human beings, they are proud of their bodies.; त्वद् अविद्यया कृतोऽयं गुण-प्रवाहः प्रवर्तते, अतो महान् विशेष इत्य् अर्थः ॥१२॥ — This flow of the modes of nature, caused by ignorance of You, is flowing, and therefore it is a great distinction, this means.
12.translation: Indeed, by saying that you are of nature, you are also speaking of my relationship with nature. Then, fearing that my chaka might be special to them, he said specially to you. For undivided vision and untainted intelligence. Where is it from? This means that the whole self is unattached to the self, since it is not separate from itself. What about the witness of all intelligence? This means that there is no ointment of intelligence anywhere because it is the witness of all intelligence. Others, he argues, are transmitted by the flow of the modes. This means that in those whose souls are demigods, human beings and human beings, they are proud of their bodies. This flow of the modes of nature, caused by ignorance of You, is flowing, and therefore it is a great distinction, this means.

13.word_for_word: सर्वात्मन इत्य् अनेनोक्तं स-गुणं स्तौति---अग्निर् मुखम् इति द्वाभ्याम् । — He praises the same quality, which is said to be of the whole soul, in two ways: fire is the mouth.; अग्न्य्-आदीन् अनूद्येश्वरावयवता विधीयते । — The fire and others are prescribed by the translating God as an organ.; योऽयम् अग्निः स तु तव मुखम् इत्य्-आदि-वचन-व्यक्त्या । — This fire is your face, etc., by the person of the words.; ईक्षणं चक्षुः । — The eye is the eye.; श्रुतिः श्रवणेन्द्रियम् । — Sruti is the sense of hearing.; कं मूर्धा । — Co. head.; प्राणश् च बलं च तत् ॥१३॥ — That is the life and strength.
13.translation: He praises the same quality, which is said to be of the whole soul, in two ways: fire is the mouth. The fire and others are prescribed by the translating God as an organ. This fire is your face, etc., by the person of the words. The eye is the eye. Sruti is the sense of hearing. Co. head. That is the life and strength.

14.word_for_word: अद्रयः परस्य तेऽस्थि-नखानि ॥१४॥ — The mountains are your bones and nails of the other.
14.translation: The mountains are your bones and nails of the other.

15.word_for_word: न केवलम् एतावत्, किन्तु सर्वोऽप्य् अयं प्रपञ्चस् त्वद्-अवयव-भूत एवेति वदन्न् एवं सत्य् अपि प्रपञ्चस्य षट् जन्मादयो विकारास् त्वयि न प्रसज्जन्ते, तस्य त्वयि कल्पितत्वाद् इत्य् आह---त्वयीति । — Not only this, but saying that the whole universe is a part of You, he argues that even though it is true that the six births and other transformations of the universe are not attached to You, because it is conceived in You.; अव्ययात्मनि पुरुषे पूर्णे लोकादयः सञ्जिहते प्रचरन्ति हे अव्ययात्मन्न् इति वा । — In the inexhaustible Self, when the Supreme Person is complete, the worlds and other things are moving about, or, O inexhaustible Self.; क्थं-भूते त्वयि । — Ktham-bhute in you.; मनो-मये मनः प्रधाने मनो-वृत्ति-व्यङ्ग्ये---दृश्यते त्वग्र्यया बुद्ध्या, मनसैवानुद्रष्टव्यःइत्य्-आदि-श्रुतेः । — In the mind-consciousness, the mind is the principal expression of the mind-instinct---it is seen by the skin intellect, and it is to be seen by the mind itself, according to the scriptures, etc.; जले यथा जलौकसः सूक्ष्म-प्राण्य्-अण्ड-राशयो यथा चोदुम्बरान्तः-केसरेषु मशकाः परस्पर-वार्तानभिज्ञाः, एवम् अनन्तानि ब्रह्माण्डानि त्वयि सञ्चरन्तीत्य् अर्थः ॥१५॥ — This means that just as the aquatic creatures in water, the heaps of tiny creatures and their eggs, and the mosquitoes in the hairs of the coconut tree are aware of each other's conversations, so the infinite universes move about in You, this means.
15.translation: Not only this, but saying that the whole universe is a part of You, he argues that even though it is true that the six births and other transformations of the universe are not attached to You, because it is conceived in You. In the inexhaustible Self, when the Supreme Person is complete, the worlds and other things are moving about, or, O inexhaustible Self. Ktham-bhute in you. In the mind-consciousness, the mind is the principal expression of the mind-instinct---it is seen by the skin intellect, and it is to be seen by the mind itself, according to the scriptures, etc. This means that just as the aquatic creatures in water, the heaps of tiny creatures and their eggs, and the mosquitoes in the hairs of the coconut tree are aware of each other's conversations, so the infinite universes move about in You, this means.

16.word_for_word: तस्माद् एवं-भूतं तव स्वरूपं दुरवगाहम् इति त्वद्-अवतार-कथामृतम् एव सन्तः सेवन्त इत्य् आह---यानि यानीति । — Therefore, it is argued that the saints serve only the nectar of the story of Your incarnation, for Your form, which is thus formed, is difficult to understand.; आमृष्टा परिमार्जिता शुक् येषां ते ॥१६॥ — They are unclean and wiped dry.
16.translation: Therefore, it is argued that the saints serve only the nectar of the story of Your incarnation, for Your form, which is thus formed, is difficult to understand. They are unclean and wiped dry.

17.word_for_word: अतः स्वयम् अप्य् अवतारान् नमस्यति, नम इति । — Therefore, he himself bows down to the incarnations, saying, “Obeisance.”; हयशीर्षे हयग्रीवाय । — to the horse’s head and horse’s neck.; मधु-कैटभयोर् मृत्यवे हन्त्रे ॥१७॥ — Destroyer of the death of Madhu and Kaitabha.
17.translation: Therefore, he himself bows down to the incarnations, saying, “Obeisance.” to the horse’s head and horse’s neck. Destroyer of the death of Madhu and Kaitabha.

18.word_for_word: अकूपाराय कूर्माय । — Acupara, the tortoise.; क्षित्य्-उद्धारो विहारो यस्य तस्मै ॥१८.१९॥ — To him whose pastime is the lifting of the earth.
18.translation: Acupara, the tortoise. To him whose pastime is the lifting of the earth.

20.word_for_word: भृगूणां पतये परशुरामाय ॥२०॥ — O Parasurama lord of the Bhrigus
20.translation: O Parasurama lord of the Bhrigus

21.word_for_word: चतुर्-व्यूह--रूपेण प्रणमति, नमस् ते वासुदेवायेति ॥२१॥ — He bows down in the form of four clusters, saying, 'Obeisances to you, O Vasudeva.
21.translation: He bows down in the form of four clusters, saying, 'Obeisances to you, O Vasudeva.

23.word_for_word: एवं स्तुत्वा बन्ध-मोक्षं प्रार्थयितुम् आह---भगवन्न् इति । — After thus praising the Lord, he prayed for liberation from bondage and liberation.; असति देहादौ ग्राह आग्रहो यस्य सः, असन् ग्राहो यस्येति वा ॥२३॥ — He who has the urge to grasp the body in the beginning of non-existence, or whose grasp is non-existent.
23.translation: After thus praising the Lord, he prayed for liberation from bondage and liberation. He who has the urge to grasp the body in the beginning of non-existence, or whose grasp is non-existent.

24.word_for_word: न केवलम् अयं लोकोऽहम् अपि तथैवेत्य् आह---अहं चेति ॥२४॥ — Not only this world, but also I, he argues, and I.
24.translation: Not only this world, but also I, he argues, and I.

25.word_for_word: मूढत्वम् एव प्रकटयति, विपर्यय-मतिर् इति । — It reveals only stupidity, that is, the mind of the opposite.; अनित्ये कर्म-फले नित्यम् इति, अनात्मनि देहे आत्मेति, दुःख-रूपे गृहादौ सुखम् इति विपरीत-मतिर् इत्य् अर्थः । — This means that the opposite mind is that the fruit of action is eternal in the impermanent, that the self is in the body without the self, and that happiness in the form of suffering is in the house and so on.; द्वन्द्वेषु सुख-दुःखादिष्व् आरमति क्रीडतीति तथा सः । — He enjoys and plays in the dualities of pleasure and pain.; ननु दुःखे कुतो रतिस् तत्राह---तमो-विष्टस् तमसा व्याप्तोऽत आत्मनः प्रियं प्रेमास्पदं त्वा त्वां न जान इत्य् अर्थः ॥२५॥ — If so, where is the attraction to suffering? He says, "I am enveloped in darkness and pervaded by darkness; therefore I do not know You, the dearest of the Self, the object of love.
25.translation: It reveals only stupidity, that is, the mind of the opposite. This means that the opposite mind is that the fruit of action is eternal in the impermanent, that the self is in the body without the self, and that happiness in the form of suffering is in the house and so on. He enjoys and plays in the dualities of pleasure and pain. If so, where is the attraction to suffering? He says, "I am enveloped in darkness and pervaded by darkness; therefore I do not know You, the dearest of the Self, the object of love.

26.word_for_word: तद् एव स-दृष्टान्तम् आह---यथेति । — That is the same illustration he argues: as.; तस्माज् जलाद् उद्भवन्तीति तद्-उद्भवानि तृणादीनि, तैः । — Therefore, the grass and other things that grow from the water, by them.; तथा माया-च्छन्नं त्वा त्वाम् अहं हित्वा पराङ्-मुखो देहाभिमुखो वर्त इति ॥२६॥ — Thus, covered by illusion, I have left Thee and turned towards the other and turned towards the body.
26.translation: That is the same illustration he argues: as. Therefore, the grass and other things that grow from the water, by them. Thus, covered by illusion, I have left Thee and turned towards the other and turned towards the body.

27.word_for_word: नन्व् एवं जानतः कुतो विषयाभिमुखता ? — Knowing this, then, where is the orientation towards objects?; तत्राह---नोत्सह इति । — There he says, "Not enthusiastic.; कृपणा विषय-वासना-युक्ता धीर् यस्य सः । — He whose patience is filled with miserable objects and desires; अत एव काम-कर्मभ्यां हतं क्षुभितम् इन्द्रियैश् च बलिभिर् विषय-संयुक्तैर् इतस् तत आकृष्यमाणं मनो रोद्धुं नियन्तुं न शक्नोमीति ॥२७॥ — That is why I am unable to restrain my mind, which is destroyed by lust and action, agitated by the strong senses and attracted here and there by sense gratification.
27.translation: Knowing this, then, where is the orientation towards objects? There he says, "Not enthusiastic. He whose patience is filled with miserable objects and desires That is why I am unable to restrain my mind, which is destroyed by lust and action, agitated by the strong senses and attracted here and there by sense gratification.

28.word_for_word: तद् एवम् अस्वतन्त्रो यः सोऽहं तवाङ्घ्रिं उपगतः शरणं प्राप्तः । — That is why I, who am thus unfree, have come to Your feet and have taken refuge in You.; नन्व् इन्द्रिय-परतन्त्रस्यैतद् अपि कुतस् तत्राह---तच् चापीति । — Now, where is this also for the sense-other independent?; हे ईश अन्तर्यामिन्, त्वद्-अङ्घ्र्य्-उपगमनं चासतां दुरापम्, अतो भवतोऽनुग्रह एवेत्य् अहं मन्ये । — O Lord of the innermost, it is difficult for the unrighteous to come to Your feet, and I think that it is Your grace.; अनुग्रहे सतीति वा । — or in grace, Sati.; ननु सतां सेवयेदं भवतीति किं मद्-अनुग्रहेणेत्य् अत आह---पुंस इति । — If this is done by serving the virtuous, what is it by My grace?; जीवस्य संसारस्यापवर्गः समाप्तिर् यदा त्वत्-कृपया भवेत् सम्भावनास्पदं भवति, हे अब्ज-नाभ, तदा सद्-उपासना संपद्यते, तयैव त्वयि मतिर् भवेत् त्वत्-कृपां विना न सत्-सेवा, नत्रान् त्वन्-मतिः, नतमां मुक्तिर् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२८॥ — When the liberation and completion of the world of the living entity becomes possible by Your grace, O lotus-naveled one, then the worship of the truth is attained, and by that one should concentrate on You. Without Your grace there is no true service.
28.translation: That is why I, who am thus unfree, have come to Your feet and have taken refuge in You. Now, where is this also for the sense-other independent? O Lord of the innermost, it is difficult for the unrighteous to come to Your feet, and I think that it is Your grace. or in grace, Sati. If this is done by serving the virtuous, what is it by My grace? When the liberation and completion of the world of the living entity becomes possible by Your grace, O lotus-naveled one, then the worship of the truth is attained, and by that one should concentrate on You. Without Your grace there is no true service.

29.word_for_word:
पादयोः पतन् प्रार्थयते, नम इति द्वयेन । — Falling at his feet, he prays, saying, “Obeisance” in two ways.; विज्ञणम् एव मात्रा मूर्तिर् यस्य तस्मै । — Knowledge is the only thing that is the idol of the matter.; अत एव सर्व-प्रत्यय-हेतवे समस्त-ज्ञान-कारणाय । — That is why He is the cause of all belief and the cause of all knowledge.; किं च पुरुषस्य ये ईशाः सुख-दुःखादि-प्रापकाः काल-कर्म-स्वभावादयस् तेषां प्रधानाय नियन्त्रे । — Moreover, the gods who are the causes of happiness and distress for man, such as time, action and nature, are under the control of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.; कुतः ? — Where is it from?; ब्रह्मणे परिपूर्णाय । — to the perfect Brahman.; किं च अनन्त-शक्तये अनन्ताः शक्तयो यस्य । — What about the infinite power of the One who has infinite powers?; यद्वा अनन्त मायाख्या शक्तिर् यस्य तस्मै । — or to the one who has the power called infinite illusion.; अथवा प्रधानं प्रकृतिः पुरुषस् तत् प्रवर्तकः, ईशः काल एतत् त्रितयात्मने ब्रह्मणे । — Or rather, the principal nature is the person who initiates it, and the Lord is time, and this is the Trinity, the Brahman.; वक्ष्यति च भगवान्--- — And the Lord will say; > प्रकृतिर् ह्य् अस्योपादानमाधारः पुरुषः परः । — > Nature is the means, the basis, and the Supreme Person.; >
> सतोऽभिव्यञ्जकः कालो ब्रह्म तत् त्रितयं त्व् अहम् ॥ — >
> Time is the expression of the truth, and I am the Absolute Truth.; इति ॥२९॥ — It is said.
29.translation:
Falling at his feet, he prays, saying, “Obeisance” in two ways. Knowledge is the only thing that is the idol of the matter. That is why He is the cause of all belief and the cause of all knowledge. Moreover, the gods who are the causes of happiness and distress for man, such as time, action and nature, are under the control of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Where is it from? to the perfect Brahman. What about the infinite power of the One who has infinite powers? or to the one who has the power called infinite illusion. Or rather, the principal nature is the person who initiates it, and the Lord is time, and this is the Trinity, the Brahman. And the Lord will say > Nature is the means, the basis, and the Supreme Person. >
> Time is the expression of the truth, and I am the Absolute Truth. It is said.

30.word_for_word: सर्व-प्रत्यय-हेतुत्वम् अभिव्यञ्जयं स्तौति, नमस् त इति । — He praises the expression as the cause of all beliefs, saying, “Obeisance to you.”; वासुदेवाय चित्ताधिष्ठात्रे । — O Vāsudeva, the master of the mind.; सर्व-भूत-क्षयाय । — for the destruction of all beings.; क्षय आश्रयः । — Decay is the shelter.; अहङ्कारश् च प्राणिनाम् आश्रयः । — Ego is also the refuge of living beings.; ततश् चाहङ्काराधिष्ठात्रे सङ्कर्षणायेत्य् अर्थः । — Then, it means, for the Lord of the ego, the Lord of the universe.; हृषीकेशेति बुद्धि-मनसोर् अधिष्ठात्रोः प्रद्युम्नानिरुद्धयोर् एकी-कृत्य ग्रहणम् । — Hṛṣīkeśa is the unified grasp of Pradyumna and Aniruddha, the masters of intelligence and mind.; शरणागतं मां पाहीति प्रार्थना ॥३०॥ — Protect me who have taken refuge in you, prayer.
30.translation: He praises the expression as the cause of all beliefs, saying, “Obeisance to you.” O Vāsudeva, the master of the mind. for the destruction of all beings. Decay is the shelter. Ego is also the refuge of living beings. Then, it means, for the Lord of the ego, the Lord of the universe. Hṛṣīkeśa is the unified grasp of Pradyumna and Aniruddha, the masters of intelligence and mind. Protect me who have taken refuge in you, prayer.
